title: Production Patterns
summary: Logging, pagination, rate limiting, caching, and handling long-running tasks.

sections.content: For structured JSON logs (ELK/Cloudwatch), use structlog or python-json-logger. In production: request-ID middleware, correlation IDs, never log passwords/tokens/PII.
For large tables, use cursor-based (keyset) pagination: WHERE id > :cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT :n — performs better than OFFSET on large tables.

from slowapi import Limiter, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)
app.state.limiter = limiter

@app.get("/items/")
@limiter.limit("100/minute")
def list_items(request: Request): ...

sections.title: Rate limiting tips
sections.content: Key by user ID instead of IP for authenticated routes. For serious scale, use Redis-backed limits or an API gateway (Kong, nginx).

sections.title: Cache at the service layer
sections.content: Cache at the service layer, not the endpoint. Always set TTLs. Invalidate on writes to the affected keys.
Don't do it in the request path. Options:

items: Validate everything: path, query, body, files (type + size + streaming)
Parameterize DB access via ORM — never string-format SQL
Set security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options) via middleware

sections.title: Mount order matters
sections.content: Mount static files at a sub-path (/static), never at / first — it would shadow your routes.

quiz.question: What is the recommended way to handle long-running work?
options: Run it in the request handler
quiz.explanation: Task queues provide retries, scheduling, result tracking, and independent worker scaling. They're the standard for email, reports, ML inference, and ETL.

quiz.question: What is cursor-based pagination and why use it?
options: WHERE id > :cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT :n — faster than OFFSET on large tables
It's the same as offset pagination
quiz.explanation: Cursor-based (keyset) pagination uses WHERE id > :cursor instead of OFFSET. It's O(1) regardless of page, while OFFSET is O(n) — it must skip n rows.

quiz.question: Where should you cache data?
quiz.explanation: Cache at the service layer (before DB access), not the endpoint. Always set TTLs and invalidate on writes to the affected keys.

quiz.question: What should you never log in production?
quiz.explanation: Never log passwords, tokens, secrets, or PII. Use structured logging with request IDs and correlation IDs, but sanitize sensitive fields.

quiz.question: How should you mount static files?
quiz.explanation: Mount at a sub-path (/static). Mounting at / would shadow all your API routes — the static file handler would catch everything first.
